```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reiod)
grp <- eiod_age_sex_group(eiod_demo$age, eiod_demo$sex)
```

**The question:** is this diet both healthy *and* environmentally sound?

Both composites combine a **diet quality** criterion (GDQS ≥ 23) with an
**environmental** criterion. They differ only in the second:

| | Table | Diet quality | Environment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HESD** — healthy, environmentally sustainable diet | 5a | GDQS ≥ 23 | biodiversity below the **absolute** Table 3 threshold |
| **HDLEI** — healthy diet, low environmental impact | 5b | GDQS ≥ 23 | biodiversity below the **relative** P30 |

Neither composite defines a new cut-off. They call `eiod_absolute_threshold()`
and `eiod_relative_band()` internally, so there is no second copy of any
number anywhere in the package.

```{r}
grp <- eiod_age_sex_group(eiod_demo$age, eiod_demo$sex)
```

**`reiod` does not calculate the GDQS.** You supply it.

## A. One respondent

```{r}
# 40-year-old man, GDQS 28, biodiversity 5e-13 PDF*year
eiod_hesd(biodiversity = 5e-13, gdqs = 28, group = 4)
eiod_hdlei(biodiversity = 5e-13, gdqs = 28, group = 4)
```

## B. Vectors from your data

```{r}
table(eiod_hesd(eiod_demo$biodiv_pdf, eiod_demo$gdqs, grp))
```

Note the message about respondents under 2 years. The methods paper restricts
the composites to ages 2 and over, because the GDQS has not been validated
below that age — Table 5a prints six demographic columns, not eight. If your
sample includes under-twos, **decide explicitly whether they belong in the
denominator**, because it changes every percentage you report.

## C. The two criteria separately

Usually what you want for reporting:

```{r}
parts <- eiod_hesd(eiod_demo$biodiv_pdf, eiod_demo$gdqs, grp,
                   form = "components")
head(parts, 4)
```

`healthy` and `env` are the two sub-indicators; `category` is the four-way
Table 5a classification; `binary` is category 1 against everything else. The
sub-indicators come from `eiod_healthy_diet()` and `eiod_sustainable_diet()`,
which are exported so you can report either on its own:

```{r}
round(100 * c(
  healthy     = mean(eiod_healthy_diet(eiod_demo$gdqs), na.rm = TRUE),
  sustainable = mean(eiod_sustainable_diet(eiod_demo$biodiv_pdf, grp),
                     na.rm = TRUE),
  low_impact  = mean(eiod_low_impact(eiod_demo$biodiv_pdf, grp), na.rm = TRUE)
), 1)
```

## D. Adding both to a data frame

```{r}
d <- eiod_demo
d$group <- eiod_age_sex_group(d$age, d$sex)
d$hesd  <- eiod_hesd(d$biodiv_pdf,  d$gdqs, d$group, form = "binary")
d$hdlei <- eiod_hdlei(d$biodiv_pdf, d$gdqs, d$group, form = "binary")

head(d[, c("id", "group", "gdqs", "biodiv_pdf", "hesd", "hdlei")], 5)
```

## The thing to know before reporting these: HDLEI is nested inside HESD

```{r}
table(HESD = d$hesd, HDLEI = d$hdlei, useNA = "ifany")
```

The empty cell is **structural**, not a quirk of this sample. For biodiversity
the relative P30 cut-off sits below the absolute threshold in every
demographic group, by the same constant factor:

```{r}
vapply(1:8, function(g) {
  unname(eiod_lookup_cutoff("biodiv", g, "abs")) /
    unname(eiod_lookup_cutoff("biodiv", g, "rel", 30))
}, numeric(1))
```

Both are the same all-population figure scaled by the same energy-requirement
weight, so the ratio is constant by construction. Every HDLEI diet is
therefore also a HESD diet, and HESD prevalence can never fall below HDLEI
prevalence.

Reporting both is still informative — the gap between them is the share of
diets sitting between the two cut-offs — but **they are not two independent
dimensions and must not be presented as a 2×2.**

## Only one indicator is involved

Unlike Tables 3 and 4, the composites use **biodiversity only**. There is no
subset to choose and no batch form, because there is nothing to batch: the
paper defines these two metrics on that one indicator.
